title: Setting, spacing and grouting
audience: Tilers who set tiles to a finished standard and grout them, and are paid for the higher-rate work
learningOutcomes: Set tiles with even spacing and a level finish across the area.
Achieve full adhesive coverage behind each tile.
Grout joints to the grout's data sheet and clean the surface without damaging it.

instruction.heading: Before the first tile goes down
instruction.body: Setting is only as good as the bed and the layout beneath it. Confirm that the substrate has been assessed and prepared as set out in “Tile types, substrate assessment and waterproofing boundary”, and that the area is clean, dry and within the moisture limit that the adhesive data sheet gives. Dry-lay the tiles from the chosen centre line or main line so that the cut tiles at the edges are a sensible size. Check the tile batch for shade and size variation before opening the boxes, because a mixed batch can show across a floor. Mix only the adhesive that can be used within its open time, and read that time from the data sheet rather than from habit. Choose the trowel notch for the tile size and the bed thickness that the data sheet gives. A larger tile usually needs a deeper bed, but the actual figures come from the product.

instruction.heading: Spacing, level and lippage
instruction.body: Use spacers of one consistent width across the area so that the joints run straight and even. The joint width depends on the tile, its edge profile and the grout the data sheet allows, so set it before you start rather than adjusting it tile by tile. Check the face level of each tile against its neighbour with a straight edge laid across the joint, or with a lippage gauge where one is used. Lippage is the step between adjacent tile edges. It can be felt underfoot and it catches the light, so it is checked while the adhesive is still workable. If a tile sits proud, lift it and re-set it while the bed is open. Do not tap a tile down into a bed that is already skinning over, because that pushes the adhesive out and leaves a void behind. Write the finish tolerance in the quote or the task sheet in a form that can be measured, such as a stated gap under a straight edge of a stated length. The numbers must be set for the job and the tile. The format is an example only; no tolerance figure is given in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Adhesive coverage and back-buttering
instruction.body: Coverage is the share of the tile back that is in contact with adhesive, and it matters more than speed. Lift a sample tile at intervals, for example after each small section, and look at the back. Contact should show across the area that the data sheet requires, with the adhesive ridges combed in one direction so that air is not trapped. Large tiles, heavy stone and tiles in wet or heavily walked areas usually need back-buttering as well, where the data sheet asks for it. Tap each tile with the handle of a tool after it is set. A solid sound suggests a full bed. A hollow or drummy sound means a void, and that tile is lifted and re-bedded while the adhesive is workable. Hollow areas crack under foot traffic or when the substrate moves. A crack that appears later is far harder to explain than a sample lift taken now, and the record of the lift is the evidence that the bed was checked.

instruction.heading: Choosing and mixing the grout
instruction.body: Choose the grout type and colour from the tile, the joint width and the use of the area. Check the data sheet for the joint widths the product is designed for. Cement-based grout and epoxy grout behave differently. They need different mixing, working time, cleaning and curing, and some tile faces are sensitive to some products. Mix to the ratio on the data sheet, and measure the water and the powder rather than estimating them. Mix only the amount you can use within the working time. Do not add water to a grout that has begun to stiffen unless the data sheet allows it. If the data sheet calls for a slaking or rest period before the final mix, allow it. Keep grout from different batches apart, or mix them together only if the product allows it, because a shade difference will show across a finished floor.

instruction.heading: Grouting, finishing and cleaning
instruction.body: Press grout into the joints with a rubber float held at an angle, working diagonally across the joints so that the grout is forced into the gap and the joint fills without voids. Work in small areas that you can finish within the working time. Remove the excess from the tile faces as the data sheet directs, using the float at the stage it names, and do not let grout dry into a haze on the face. Clean the surface with a damp sponge and a clean water change. Rinse the sponge often, because a dirty sponge spreads grout back over the tiles. Polish the surface only with the cloth or product the data sheet names. Natural stone, unglazed tile and some glazed finishes can be marked or etched by acid-based cleaners, so use only the cleaner the data sheet allows. Where the data sheet calls for it, test a hidden area first. Sealing, where it is part of the job, is a separate step with its own data sheet and is not covered here.

instruction.heading: Curing, inspection and the finished record
instruction.body: Keep foot traffic off the floor, and keep the area dry, for the cure time the data sheet gives. Once the grout has cured, look along the joints in good light for pinholes, shrinkage, low spots and unfilled sections. If the data sheet allows a repair with the same product, fill and finish the defect and record it. Take the finish inspection photographs with the client's permission. If a void or a hollow is found after grouting, record the location, the cause if it is known, and the repair. Do not describe the repair as a guarantee of the floor, because the record shows only what was checked on the day.

procedure: Confirm the substrate has been assessed and is within the moisture limit on the adhesive data sheet.
Dry-lay the tiles from the centre or main line, and check the batch for shade and size.
Mix only the adhesive that can be used within its open time, and set spacers of one width.
Check each tile's level against its neighbour with a straight edge while the adhesive is workable, and re-set any tile that sits proud.
Lift a sample tile at intervals to check adhesive coverage, and back-butter large or heavy tiles where the data sheet requires it.
Tap each set tile, and re-bed any tile that sounds hollow before the area is grouted.
Allow the adhesive to set for the data sheet time before grouting.
Mix grout to the data sheet ratio, and press it into the joints diagonally, filling without voids.
Remove the excess and clean the surface with a damp sponge and a clean water change at the stage the data sheet gives.
Keep traffic off for the cure time, then inspect the joints for voids, pinholes and low spots, and record the result.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A floor of large tiles is grouted, and a sound check afterwards finds a hollow tile in the middle of the room. The client asks you to grout the rest as planned to meet a handover date.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the grouting continue as planned, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop grouting in the affected area and check the hollow tile before going on. If the grout is still soft, clear the joints around the tile and lift it, then check the coverage on the back. If the grout has set, the joints around the tile have to be opened before the tile can be lifted. Either way, the bed is re-applied where coverage is poor, and the tile is re-set and levelled. Continue grouting only once the bed is confirmed, because a hollow tile will crack under load. Tell the client that the affected area takes longer, and do not promise the handover date until the fix is complete. Record the check, the cause if it is known, and the fix, with a photograph taken with permission. The sequence is an example of the decision; the times and the method are set by the job and the data sheet.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A honed natural stone floor shows a grout haze after grouting. The owner asks you to use a strong acid-based bathroom cleaner to clear it quickly.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which cleaner do you use, and what do you check first?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the acid-based cleaner unless the stone and grout data sheets allow it. Ask for the data sheets, identify a cleaner that the data sheet names, and test it on a hidden area first. Clean with a damp sponge and clean water, changing the water often and rinsing the sponge. If the haze has already dried, use the removal method the data sheet gives rather than scrubbing hard, which can mark the surface. Record the product, the test area and the result. If the owner still wants the acid-based product, record the request, explain the risk, and do not use it.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) In a warm, sunny room the grout is drying faster than planned, and a haze is forming on the glazed tile faces before you reach the last section.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you change, and what do you do with the haze already present?
workedExamples.reasoning: Work in smaller sections so that each one can be finished within the working time. Clean the haze at the stage the data sheet gives, not later. Where the data sheet cautions about heat, draughts or direct sun, shade the area or change the timing. Record the conditions and the change to the method. For haze that has already dried, follow the data sheet's removal method and test a small area first, rather than scrubbing the glaze, which can dull it.

equipmentAndPpe: Spacers of one consistent width for the tile and joint
Straight edge, and a lippage gauge where one is used
Notched trowel sized to the tile, and a back-buttering trowel for large or heavy tiles
Rubber grout float, a clean mixing bucket and a mixing paddle
Measures for water and powder, as the data sheet directs
Damp sponge, two clean buckets and a clean cloth for finishing
Tool handle for the tap test, and a tape measure and pencil for the set-out
Eye protection, waterproof gloves and knee pads
Dust mask or respirator for dry powder mixing, selected to the product label and SDS and used after the wet and ventilation controls are in place

commonErrors.prevention: Tap each set tile, lift and re-bed any hollow tile, and record the fix before grouting the area.

commonErrors.error: Setting the whole area without a sample lift, so coverage is unknown.
commonErrors.prevention: Lift sample tiles at intervals while the adhesive is workable and record the result.

commonErrors.error: Using an acid-based cleaner on natural stone or unglazed tile.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the cleaner the data sheet allows, and test a hidden area first where the data sheet asks for it.

commonErrors.error: Leaving grout haze to dry on the tile face.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean the haze with a damp sponge and clean water at the stage the data sheet gives, working in sections.

commonErrors.error: Adding water to grout that has started to stiffen.
commonErrors.prevention: Mix only what can be used within the working time, and do not add water unless the data sheet allows it.

commonErrors.error: Tapping a proud tile down into a bed that is skinning over.
commonErrors.prevention: Lift and re-set the tile while the adhesive is workable, and recheck the level.

commonErrors.error: Grouting from mixed batches without checking the shade.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the batch of tiles and the grout before starting, and keep batches apart where the product requires it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Queensland and Victoria thresholds: in Queensland, wall and floor tiling is a QBCC licence class, and work outside that class is allowed only as incidental work valued at $3,300 or less. In Victoria, a job involving only tiling (wall and floor) needs no registration, but combining tiling with another trade on one job needs registration, and domestic building work with a contract worth more than $10,000 needs registration. Work above these limits needs the licence or registration. This lesson does not grant any of these.

New South Wales: the NSW Government page says a contractor licence or a qualified supervisor certificate is needed for wall and floor tiling work valued at more than $5,000 in labour and materials, including GST. The same page says the covered work includes waterproofing wet areas before tiling, and inserting expansion joints. The boundary with a waterproofer must therefore be confirmed on each job, and not assumed.
Floating floors and vinyl are not named on the NSW tiling page. This lesson does not extend the NSW licence position to floating floors; see “Floating floor installation (underlay, expansion gaps)”.
Completing this lesson does not give a tiling licence, certificate or authority in any state or territory, and it does not authorise waterproofing or structural work.

Adhesives, grouts, sealers and cleaners may be hazardous chemicals. Each product used should have a current safety data sheet. A compliant SDS has 16 headings, including hazards, first aid, handling and storage, exposure controls and disposal. A copy can be obtained from the supplier at no cost on first supply or on request, and an SDS should have been prepared within the last five years. The workplace hazardous chemicals register must list the current SDS for each hazardous chemical kept there, and it must be readily accessible.

Control hazards before relying on personal protective equipment. The WorkSafe Victoria hierarchy of control lists elimination first and personal protective equipment last, as the least reliable control. In practice this means wet mixing and ventilation come before a respirator for grout powder.

Bags of grout and adhesive, and boxes of tiles, are heavy. Safe Work Australia's model Code of Practice on hazardous manual tasks says that manual tasks must be identified, their risks assessed and the risks managed.

AS 3958.1 (installation of ceramic tiles) was located as a seller listing only. Dust from dry grout powder and from tile cutting is covered in “Cutting tile and silica dust controls”, which is not verified here.

qualityStandard: Tiles are set level and evenly spaced, within the tolerance written in the task sheet, with a sample lift showing the adhesive coverage the data sheet requires.
Any hollow tile found by sound is lifted, checked and re-bedded before grouting in that area.
Grout is mixed to the data sheet ratio and fills every joint without voids.
Haze is removed at the stage the data sheet gives, and no acid-based cleaner is used on natural stone or unglazed tile unless the data sheet allows it.
Joints are inspected after cure, and any defect is recorded with its location and repair.
documentationEvidence: Setting and coverage check record, with the sample lift photographs taken with permission
Adhesive and grout product record, with the data sheet reference and batch numbers
Mix record, showing the water and powder quantities and the time mixed
Repair record for any tile re-bedded or joint re-filled
Finish inspection record taken after the grout has cured
summary: Set tiles with spacers, check level and lippage, and sample-lift the coverage while the adhesive is workable.
Re-bed any hollow tile before grouting, and never grout over a suspect area.
Mix and grout to the data sheet, and clean the haze at the stage the data sheet gives.
Use only the cleaners the data sheet allows on natural stone and unglazed tile, and record the work.

knowledgeChecks.question: A hollow sound is found under one tile before grouting. What is correct?
options: Grout over it and check the tile later on in the week or the month after
Tap it and leave it as it sits in place for the grouting and the whole job
Lift the tile, check the adhesive coverage, and re-bed it before grouting
Fill the hollow with grout from the bucket and smooth it over well today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which cleaner should be avoided on natural stone unless the data sheet allows it?
Why is the sample lift done while the adhesive is still workable?
options: So the tile can be lifted and re-set if the coverage or level is poor
So the grout can be mixed and spread on the tile at once today
So the tile can be cut to size before it is set on the floor today
It is not needed once the tile is set in the bed and the grout is in

knowledgeChecks.question: The grout is starting to stiffen in the bucket. What should you do?
options: Add water to loosen it, whatever the data sheet says, since the grout is too stiff to use
Add water only if the data sheet allows it, otherwise mix a fresh batch within the working time
Keep it and grout anyway with the batch as it is, since it is nearly ready to use
Add more powder to thicken the mix and keep going on the job today with the crew
